title: Update existing web notification

labels.name: needs implementer interest
labels.description: Moving the issue forward requires implementers to express interest

body:
### What problem are you trying to solve?

On my platform my Mail Module cycles through email addresses in the primary loop and then each folder ("mail box") in a second loop per primary loop iteration. Each folder creates an additional secondary iteration. It can take 3-20 seconds to import new messages. However it might only take 1.2 seconds before I have all of the messages from the first inbox as my platform allows changing the order of which Mail Accounts can be checked/imported. Often 10-20 seconds of extra time can have a meaningful impact in business.

### What solutions exist today?

Either none of simply spamming a modified version of the notification.

### How would you solve it?

It would be extremely helpful in this scenario if I could simply update an _existing_ web notification. When the inboxes for other Mail Accounts have additional messages I'd rather simply update an existing notification. This would allow me to trigger the web notification several seconds earlier and then instead of spamming them (let's say, new messages for five different Mail Accounts) it would simply update the same notification.

This should be easily achievable by allowing each notification to have a unique id as defined in the second parameter options object. Here is a rough example:

`new Notification('Example', {body: 'You have new messages', id: 'mail_new_'+Date.now()});`

It's clear between Waterfox and Vivaldi that the notifications are still directly controlled by the browser. I can easily live with the platforms taking a little longer to implement updates.

### Anything else?

### Real World Use-Case

I have business meetings fairly frequently and most people are _not_ organized. So sometimes they will reschedule _only after_ receiving an email reminder 30-60 minutes before the already agreed to meeting.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/bbbedcdd-0813-4b3b-b5c7-2acfecb485d6)

I think a large portion of people in these scenarios have their hands full and need all of the advanced notice to know if the other person in your one-on-one will be a no-show and thus recovering one's time to stay productive sooner than later. When considerable money is on the line and being able to hire more people depends on improving time-efficiency the justification is definitely there.
